title: LEGO celebrates SpongeBob's 40th with new set and retro-style intro

bodyMarkdown:

To celebrate, the LEGO Group recreated the show's iconic theme song intro using minifigures and pieces from the new set, reportedly even including a LEGO version of Painty the Pirate's painting from the original sequence. SpongeBob is one of LEGO's longest-running licensed themes, and anniversary sets like this often become popular with collectors and nostalgic fans. A fun, well-produced promo like the recreated intro also shows how LEGO continues to lean into pop culture nostalgia to market its licensed builds.

title: LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants Returns After 14 Years
summary: LEGO has officially revealed two new SpongeBob SquarePants sets, ending a 14-year gap since the theme last appeared on shelves.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially unveiled two new SpongeBob SquarePants sets: LEGO Icons 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom and 40858 SpongeBob SquarePants Figure. This marks the theme's first appearance since it ended in 2012, following an original run that began in 2006 as part of a joint Nickelodeon push alongside Avatar: The Last Airbender.

Back in 2006, SpongeBob quickly outgrew its shared Nickelodeon branding and became its own theme, eventually spanning 14 sets across three main waves. Early releases like 3825 Krusty Krab and 3826 Build-A-Bob introduced Bikini Bottom to builders, while later sets such as 4981 The Chum Bucket and 3831 Rocket Ride expanded the cast with characters like Sandy Cheeks. In 2009, LEGO revisited its earliest designs with updated versions of the Krusty Krab and pineapple house, before the theme wound down by 2012 as LEGO shifted focus to other properties like Atlantis and Hero Factory.

## Why it matters
For UK collectors and fans of nostalgic licensed themes, this is a significant official comeback. Twenty-two years after SpongeBob SquarePants first aired, and 14 years after LEGO last touched Bikini Bottom, this return could open the door to further sets if demand is strong — something display builders and IP collectors will want to watch closely.

## What to watch next
Watch for further official details on pricing, piece count and UK release dates for 11386 and 40858, plus any hints about whether more Bikini Bottom sets could follow if the relaunch proves popular.

title: LEGO Ideas designer reveals how much La Catrina shrank before release
summary: The fan behind LEGO Ideas 21372 La Catrina has shared a side-by-side comparison showing just how much the design changed from submission to final set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan designer yop1172, whose La Catrina concept was submitted to LEGO Ideas back in August 2023, has posted a comparison video showing their original build next to the official finished set.

The differences are striking. The original design stood at 86cm tall and used 2,894 pieces. The final LEGO Ideas 21372 La Catrina set, officially confirmed for release on 1 August, is 43cm tall with 1,212 pieces — less than half the size and part count of the original pitch.

Other changes include a different coloured dress and a reworked skull design. The set is priced at £109.99 / $139.99 / €119.99 and is already available to pre-order via LEGO.com.

yop1172 thanked the LEGO design team, including Jim Clayton, Melody and Jordan, for their work adapting the concept, and Clayton publicly replied on Instagram praising the original submission.

## Why it matters
This is a useful reminder that LEGO Ideas sets rarely reach shelves unchanged — official design teams often significantly rework fan submissions for cost, structural stability and display practicality. For collectors and builders, seeing the 'before and after' offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at how a huge, ambitious concept gets turned into a shippable retail product.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants returns with new Icons set

## What happened

The headline release is LEGO Icons 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom, priced at £189.99, containing 1,794 pieces and due out on 1 September 2026. It's aimed at builders aged 18+.

The set recreates the houses of SpongeBob, Squidward and Patrick on Conch Street, designed to sit side by side as a display piece. Each house has a full interior — Patrick's rock home has a TV and chair, Squidward's includes a living room, bathroom, bedroom and rooftop, and SpongeBob's features a living room and bedroom.

Fans can expect plenty of nods to the show, including Easter eggs like Penny, Chip and Used Napkin from specific episodes, plus side builds such as a boat, Jellyfish Fields, the Bikini Bottom sign, Gary and DoodleBob. The set includes three minifigures — SpongeBob, Squidward and Patrick — each with a unique character-specific piece.

A second SpongeBob set has also been revealed under a different existing LEGO theme, though full details on that model weren't included in this excerpt.

## Why it matters
This marks LEGO's first SpongeBob SquarePants sets in over a decade, and the Icons format signals a clear pitch to adult fans and collectors rather than just younger viewers. For display-build enthusiasts, the modular-style houses with detailed interiors and nostalgic Easter eggs make this a strong addition to any nostalgic or pop-culture display collection.

title: Fan-built Star Wars freighter is designed to swallow the LEGO Millennium Falcon whole
summary: Builder Sentinel_Brix has created an original Star Wars-style ship, the Savareena, big enough to fit LEGO's 75375 Millennium Falcon inside it — a fan creation, not an official LEGO set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Over on The Brothers Brick, fan builder Sentinel_Brix has shown off an original custom LEGO creation called the Savareena — a large freighter built for the Star Wars: Factions role-play community.

Despite being a completely new design rather than a real Star Wars vehicle, the ship is packed with the kind of detailed panelling ("greebles") that instantly reads as Star Wars. The real showstopper is the concept behind it: the Savareena was designed specifically to be big enough to fit the official LEGO 75375 Millennium Falcon set inside its hull. Sentinel_Brix backed this up with a photo spread styled like the official Star Wars Visual Dictionary books, showing the Falcon tucked away inside the larger ship.

The build also includes a nice nod to another LEGO product line, incorporating the Planets series Death Star model as part of the scene.

This is a fan-made MOC ("my own creation") shared via The Brothers Brick and is not an official LEGO Group product or announcement.

## Why it matters
This kind of build is a great example of how existing LEGO sets can spark entirely new ideas — using an official model as both inspiration and a literal design constraint. For stadium and large-scale display builders especially, it's a useful reminder that scale, storage, and "ship-in-a-ship" style engineering challenges can drive genuinely creative custom projects.

title: Rumoured LEGO Star Wars cinema set has a long line of LEGO movie theatres before it
summary: Chatter about a possible LEGO Star Wars cinema set for 2027 has us looking back at the LEGO cinemas that have already graced our shelves, from 2008's Town Plan to the beloved Palace Cinema modular.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

According to these rumours, it would be an 18+ set retailing at $199.99 in the US and arriving on 1 April 2027 — but none of this has been officially confirmed by LEGO, so treat it as speculation for now.

The most famous LEGO cinema followed in **2013 with 10232 Palace Cinema**, a 2,196-piece modular building inspired by Hollywood's Chinese Theatre. It featured a four-walled interior with room for six minifigures at the screen, plus posters for in-universe films — and US buyers in September 2013 even got a bonus poster referencing The LEGO Movie.

A smaller entry came in **2014 with 40180 Bricktober Theater**, a 164-piece Toys 'R' Us giveaway set continuing the cinema theme on a much smaller scale.

## Why it matters
LEGO cinema builds have a strong pedigree among modular and city fans, so a potential Star Wars-themed entry — sitting alongside multi-theme sets like Friends, Batman and Icons — would be a notable addition if confirmed. For UK collectors and display builders, it's worth keeping an eye on official announcements before getting too invested in the rumoured details.
